summary.intent: Execute phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) via wave-based parallel execution across 8 plans, then run the ship-phase workflow (verify, secure, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit, ship) to get the PR up and through CI.
summary.outcome: All 7 code plans completed and committed with a full local gate (351 Rust + 252 sdk-core + 172 API jest + 89 SDK E2E all green); the SDK E2E gate caught a real ship-blocking regression from 60-05 which was diagnosed and fixed; phase 60-08 (staging cutover) is paused pending human-action; session ended before the PR was opened due to the 1Password signing wedge.

repo: Ed25519 IPNS records do NOT embed pubKey in the protobuf bytes — `parseIpnsRecordBytes` does not yield `pubKey` for these records; it must be supplied from the separate `FolderIpns.publicKey` DB column (which publish validates via `deriveIpnsName(publicKey) === ipnsName`).
The `subject-no-parens` commitlint rule rejects parens anywhere in the commit description subject — trailing `(D-XX)` references in executor commits break the `pr-release-preview` CI gate.
Wave executors commit `Cargo.toml` changes but not the resulting `Cargo.lock` updates, creating a latent `--locked` CI break that must be caught and committed by the orchestrator.
CAPACITY.md §1.5 was already occupied by a prior phase; executors should discover existing section numbering and use §1.6 rather than overwrite.
GSD executor commit subjects use a non-conventional `feat 60-01:` style that needs filter-branch rewording before the PR or `pr-release-preview` fails.
GSD ROADMAP checkboxes are not always updated by sequential plan executors — the orchestrator must reconcile after all waves complete.
The `gsd:phase uat-passed` CLI exists in help output but has no handler — use `edit VERIFICATION.md` + `phase complete` as the workaround.

code.finding: TS resolve path conditionally skipped EOL enforcement when the Validity field was absent (only enforced when Validity was a Uint8Array); Rust fail-closes on absent Validity via `.ok_or_else()`. Fixed to fail-closed parity (D-07-e) — a genuine cross-layer divergence the phase's strict-cutover intent required.

60-05's D-06 removal of the `withCachedPublicKey` enrich caused `resolveRecord` to return the bare network result on equal-sequence, which carries no `pubKey` for Ed25519 records. The fix: return the authoritative DB `cachedResult` (which has `pubKey`, `signatureV2`, and `data`) on equal-or-higher sequence.

The D-06 unit test mocked `parseIpnsRecord` to include `pubKey` (masking realistic Ed25519 behavior) and asserted that `signatureV2`/`data` would be `undefined` on equal-sequence — it codified the bug rather than the correct behavior. Test was updated to match the fixed contract.
Rust reference implementation: fail-closes on absent Validity via `.ok_or_else(...)` — the behavioral contract the TS D-07-e fix mirrors.
`parseCachedRecord` was updated to carry `pubKey` from the validated `publicKey` column so callers get a fully verifiable record (the strict client re-checks `deriveIpnsName(pubKey) === ipnsName`).

workflow: The SDK E2E gate is the only suite exercising the real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip; all unit suites mock the boundary and miss integration regressions — it caught a 28/89 break here that 343 unit tests (Rust + sdk-core + API jest) all missed.
SDK E2E accounts use `Date.now()`-seeded emails → unique keys per run → stale-data collision is ruled out as a failure hypothesis without needing a DB wipe.
Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the main working tree is the correct mode for crypto-cutover phases where correctness and per-plan verification gates outweigh wall-clock parallelism.
The GSD commit helper can report `commit_failed` while the commit actually landed (lint-staged output triggers a false-negative); always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

1Password SSH signing agent wedges after a burst of rapid commits (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`); recovery requires quitting and reopening the 1Password desktop app or toggling Settings → Developer → SSH agent off/on.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged after ~28 rapid commits, blocking all further commits for the duration of the SDK E2E gate run and requiring a manual app restart from the user.
The GSD commit helper's false-negative `commit_failed` pattern required manual `git log` verification after every commit, adding noise throughout the session.
Wave 1 executors left two uncommitted artifacts (stale Cargo.lock and a factually-wrong SUMMARY.md footer) that the orchestrator had to detect and clean up between waves.
60-06's ROADMAP checkbox was not ticked by its executor, requiring a reconciliation commit discovered only during the Wave 4 state inspection.

The SDK E2E gate failure (28/89) required a multi-step root-cause investigation (checking build cleanliness, harness key generation, API resolve code path, codec behavior, and DB column semantics) before a fix could be written.
